gloss: to start on; to touch; to lay a hand on

definitions.gloss: to start on; to begin working on
definitions.explanation: To begin doing something, especially a task or project that one has been putting off or hasn't addressed yet.

definitions.gloss: to touch; to lay a hand on; to tamper with
definitions.explanation: To physically touch or handle something, often with the nuance of meddling with or tampering with something one shouldn't.

examples.japanese: {宿題|しゅくだい}に{手|て}をつける。
まだその{仕事|しごと}に{手|て}をつけていない。
examples.english: I haven't started on that work yet.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しくて、{新|あたら}しいプロジェクトに{手|て}をつける{余裕|よゆう}がない。
examples.english: I'm too busy to start on the new project.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}のものに{手|て}をつけるな。
{貯金|ちょきん}に{手|て}をつけたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to dip into my savings.

examples.japanese: {証拠品|しょうこひん}に{手|て}をつけてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not tamper with the evidence.

notes:
A common idiomatic expression using {手|て} (hand) and つける (to attach/apply). The two senses are connected: both involve putting one's hand to something, whether figuratively (starting work) or literally (touching/tampering).

USAGE:
Sense 1 is very common in everyday conversation, often in the negative ({手|て}をつけていない — haven't started yet). Sense 2 often implies doing something improper, such as spending savings one shouldn't or interfering with something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事|しごと}に{手|て}をつける — to start work
- {貯金|ちょきん}に{手|て}をつける — to dip into savings
- まだ{手|て}をつけていない — haven't started yet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {取|と}りかかる — to start on, to get down to (more formal)
- {着手|ちゃくしゅ}する — to begin, to embark on (formal)
- {触|さわ}る — to touch (physical touch, neutral)
